sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: hook h1 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i01, caller. Medium target, Hard welcome (user,
  2026-10-10: no Easy slot). Edition trap in the layout that measured Medium or better on aq-00964 q01,
  aq-01322 q01 and aq-00745 q09 and Easy on aq-01333 q01 and aq-02706 q02: the event is reported only in a
  later edition, which prints its own newer same-label values; the values current at the event sit in the
  previous edition. Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 6 L156 dates the announcement July 10, 2026. Doc 6 L27 puts its own order in effect
  July 13, 2026, and L43 names the order before it (signed June 21, 2026, 30-day). Doc 5 L25-27 is that
  order: in effect June 21, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EDT, through July 21, 2026 unless replaced, so it is the one
  in force on July 10. Doc 5 L125 prints its two DRC confirmed-case counts, 91 (May 22) and 837 (June 15).
  (837 - 91) / 91 = 819.8%.
- Universe: not applicable (single value). Doc 5 prints exactly two DRC confirmed-case counts (L125); its
  other counts are Uganda's (L126).
- Necessity: Doc 6 is the only document that reports the announcement ("tested positive": Doc 6 only, one
  hit; "July 10" elsewhere is only Doc 5's comment deadline). Without it no order can be chosen among three.
  Doc 5 is the only document that prints 91 ("91 confirmed": Doc 5 only); Doc 6 restates 837 but not 91, so
  without Doc 5 the earlier count is unknown and the computable pairs are Doc 6's (123.8%) and Doc 7's
  (130.5%). The wording gives no date, count or order. Doc 7 is not needed: it mentions neither the
  announcement nor 91.
- Selected-lever checks (Python, 2026-10-10): right edition 746 / 91 = 819.78%. Wrong edition, Doc 6's own
  pair: (1,873 - 837) / 837 = 123.78%. Doc 7's pair: (4,318 - 1,873) / 1,873 = 130.54%. Rounded prose:
  Doc 5 says "an increase of more than 800 percent"; at one decimal the figure is 819.8%, so the prose does
  not answer the question. The edition choice changes the answer by 696 percentage points.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong year or edition, uses the wrong period or date) -> 123.8%, from
  Doc 6 L125, the counts printed in the document that reports the event. No measured attempts yet;
  re-declare from observed wrong answers before Submit. Considered and not declared: "Older figure inside a
  newer report" (Doc 6's restated 837 is used correctly by the wrong route as well), "Figure that must be
  computed" (the platform's definition is a period subtraction), and a rounding mode for "more than 800
  percent" (no trap in the form's list fits a rounded prose figure).
- Calculation verification: Python 2026-10-10 with exact fractions: 837 - 91 = 746; 746 / 91 = 8.197802...,
  819.8% at one decimal. No date arithmetic enters the answer; the dates only order the event and the
  orders (June 21 <= July 10 < July 13).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: 819.8 and 746 are printed nowhere. The page overview lists "91 confirmed
  cases in DRC as of May 22, 2026" and 837 under Doc 5 but neither the announcement nor the rise. Shortest
  route: find the announcement in Doc 6, see that Doc 6's order postdates it, open the June order, take its
  two counts, divide.
- Precision/readings: "rise between the two counts" as a percentage is the increase over the earlier count
  (819.8%), which is how Doc 5 itself frames it ("an increase of more than 800 percent"); the later count as
  a share of the earlier (919.8%) is not a rise. "In force when ... was announced": orders have printed
  effective times, and only the June 21 order covers July 10. The Amended Order of May 22 is not in the
  bundle and its end date is printed nowhere; the June order "continues" the suspension, so no reading makes
  another order the one in force on July 10. If a reader took the France physician case (WHO briefing of
  June 24, 2026, Doc 6 fn 9) for the event, the order in force is the same one. "U.S. aid worker" is the
  U.S. citizen "working for a humanitarian organization in DRC".
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; notes/doc-map.md coverage lines).
- Style/set review: 30 words, one sentence, one ask. q02 uses a different event (Doc 7's), a different
  value document pair (Doc 6 and Doc 7) and a date quantity; neither question states the other's order.
- Warnings answered: see the floor run recorded at hand-over.

sections.question: By what percentage, to one decimal, did DRC's confirmed cases rise between the two counts in CDC's entry-suspension order in force when a U.S. aid worker's Ebola infection was announced?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 6, factual basis, section III.B): CDC announced on July 10, 2026 that a U.S. citizen working for a humanitarian organization in DRC had tested positive for Bundibugyo virus disease, the Ebola disease of this outbreak.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 6, DATES and SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION): the order printed in Doc 6 took effect on July 13, 2026, after that announcement, so it was not yet in force. The order before it was signed on June 21, 2026 as a 30-day order.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 5, SUMMARY and DATES): that earlier order is the one printed in Doc 5. It took effect on June 21, 2026 and was to remain in effect through July 21, 2026, so it was the entry-suspension order in force when the infection was announced.

Step 4. Source input (Doc 5, factual basis, section III.B): Doc 5 cites two DRC confirmed-case counts: 91 confirmed cases on May 22, 2026, when the Amended Order was issued, and 837 confirmed cases as of June 15, 2026. Its text rounds the rise to more than 800 percent.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): the later count less the earlier count: 837 - 91 = 746.

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): that rise as a percentage of the earlier count, to one decimal: 746 / 91 = 819.8%.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong year or edition
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Wrong year or edition: Doc 6 reports the July 10 announcement beside its own counts, 837 and 1,873, but that order took effect July 13. Using them gives 123.8%. The order in force on July 10 is Doc 5's, with 91 and 837, so 819.8%.
